stem: Vela Systems adds a rule: no infrastructure change may take effect until someone can see exactly what will be added, changed, or destroyed, and approve it first. Which workflow step provides that?

choices.text: Apply the configuration directly and roll back immediately if the result turns out to be wrong.
Generate an execution plan that lists every proposed addition, change, and deletion, and have a reviewer sign off on it before anything is applied.
Have the author write a short comment in the pull request describing what they intend to change, then apply.
Ask a second, independent engineer to re-read the entire configuration file line by line for correctness and style before it is ever applied to any environment.

rationale: The key describes the plan stage, which previews every proposed addition, change, and deletion before anything is modified, matching the stated requirement directly. Applying first and rolling back afterward means the effect is discovered only after it already happened. A written PR comment is a human description that can be incomplete or wrong, not a generated list of the actual proposed changes. A line-by-line read of the configuration file does not reveal what will actually change against infrastructure that already exists.
